progress_2026_08_16.triage_correction: AC-136-3 triage found that NONE of the ten storage modules is dead. The KERNEL_BUILDER claim that storage/loom.rs and storage/retention.rs had zero external consumers was WRONG and was disproved before any deletion: loom.rs is a pure type module (86 pub items, 0 sqlx, 0 errors) reached through the storage/mod.rs glob re-export "pub use loom::*", and retention.rs is used by src/main.rs through a multi-line grouped import that a single-line grep cannot see. Nothing was deleted. A consumer grep on "storage::<module>" is unsound in Rust.
progress_2026_08_16.unblocked_since: The dominant blocker at the time of that pass - the sealed SurrealDataContext exposing only upsert_one and select_one - has since been REMOVED by the KERNEL_BUILDER. storage/surreal.rs now also provides select_all, delete_one, query_values, query_first, execute_returning and create_if_absent, all compiling clean. The next pass on this MT should therefore no longer be blocked on query expressiveness.

progress_2026_08_16.remaining_work: The KnowledgeStore trait (~180 methods) has no implementor. impl KnowledgeStore for SurrealDatabase is the single largest remaining item and is what the entire knowledge API layer is waiting on; the API modules are already re-typed to consume &dyn KnowledgeStore.

scope.summary: Port the storage modules off sqlx onto the embedded SurrealDB store. These modules were helpers of the deleted PostgresDatabase and account for 463 of the errors: storage/knowledge.rs (184), storage/fems_memory.rs (72), storage/knowledge_crdt.rs (46), plus knowledge_memory, knowledge_retrieval, kb003_storage, block_view_outbox, calendar, retention and loom. Decide per module whether it is ported into storage/surreal/ or deleted as dead PostgreSQL implementation detail: storage/loom.rs and storage/retention.rs currently have ZERO external consumers while storage/knowledge.rs has 39, so they are not all the same case. EVIDENCE: Measured from a full cargo check of handshake_core after the physical PostgreSQL removal on 2026-08-16 (log Handshake_Artifacts/handshake-test/wp012-surreal-breakage-20260816T033259Z.log): 1716 errors across 119 files. Root causes: 1493 unresolved sqlx, 152 missing migrations .sql include_bytes (since restored), 51 deleted-postgres-module references, 20 other. SEAM: The Database trait has 201 methods: 108 required and 93 with default bodies (88 of those return StorageError::NotImplemented and 5 are supports_ capability flags). storage/surreal/database.rs already implements all 108 required methods and compiles clean; 106 currently return NotImplemented. storage/surreal/schema.surql already defines 121 tables, 1414 fields and 347 indexes, and storage/surreal/documents.rs, blocks.rs, workspaces.rs and preferences.rs already implement 36 working functions - use those as the implementation pattern. Decrement DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED in database.rs in the SAME change that ports each method; the not_implemented_surface_is_declared test enforces it.

acceptance_criteria.text: No file under src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/ references sqlx.
Every Database method backing a native-editor surface is implemented against the embedded SurrealDB store, and DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED is decremented accordingly.
Each retained module is justified by a real consumer; modules with zero consumers are deleted rather than ported.
Persistence round-trips survive a store close and reopen, proving durability rather than in-memory behaviour.

proof_targets: PT-136-1: cargo check output showing zero sqlx errors under src/storage/.
PT-136-2: a round-trip test against a real embedded SurrealDB store opened at a temporary HANDSHAKE_DATA_DIR, including close and reopen.
PT-136-3: the not_implemented_surface_is_declared test green at the reduced count.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend storage port with no operator-visible surface of its own; the surfaces it restores are proven by their own microtasks.

target_entries: storage authority and persistence behaviour for the ported domain

risks: A method ported without a real-store proof can pass against a mock and still fail at runtime.
Deleting a module that still has a live consumer would silently remove a product behaviour.
minimum_controls: No method may be left returning NotImplemented while any microtask claims that behaviour works.
Every ported method needs a proof that touches a real embedded SurrealDB store, never a mock.
DECLARED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED must be decremented in the same change that ports a method.
